Review (by pi)
------------------------------------------------------------
**Summary**

This commit stages RWX (rwx.com) ports of the four GitHub Actions CI workflows under `.rwx/` (`tests.yml`, `trunk-check.yml`, `validate-assets.yml`, `trunk-impacted-targets.yml`), ahead of a follow-up PR that will delete the GHA workflows and flip `merge.required_statuses`. It also excludes `.rwx/**` from checkov in `.trunk/trunk.yaml` because checkov's `gha-*` rules misfire on RWX task-level env blocks.

I verified against the stated reference implementations (elviskahoro/sdk-python-attio `.rwx/*`) and RWX's published docs: the trigger syntax (`on.github.pull_request`/`push` with `if:`-guarded push rules), `init`/`status-checks`, `git/clone 2.2.0` leaves, the `trunk-config`/`trunk-tools` filtered tool-cache pattern, the `$RWX_ENV/PATH` propagation, and the locked-vault `cache-key: excluded` pattern all match the working reference. The uv installer checksum (`504a79f…` for `uv/0.11.29/install.sh`) and the trunk launcher checksum match what I computed independently and what the existing GHA workflows pin. Trigger conditions faithfully mirror the GHA workflows (tests/validate-assets on PR + push to `main`/`trunk-merge*`; trunk-check PR + queue pushes only, no push-to-main; impacted-targets PR-only, no path filters). The checkov exclusion is correctly scoped to `.rwx/**` and consistent with the existing `pullfrog.yml` exclusion pattern. `required_statuses` is untouched, matching the commit message's stated scope.

**Issues**

**low** — `.rwx/trunk-check.yml` (`lint` task, the `upstream="$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)"` branch). The commit message claims "The trunk-check port lints the same bases as the GitHub workflow," but for PRs it does not: the GHA workflow diffs the merge ref against its first parent (the fresh main tip), while the RWX port diffs the PR head against the fork-point merge base. Consequence: if main fixes a finding on a line after the PR forks and the PR's changes reintroduce it, the finding exists at both endpoints of the diff and is not reported as new — a regression the GHA gate would catch but the RWX gate will silently pass. The in-file comment only covers the opposite direction (main *introducing* findings). Since this becomes a required status at cutover, the gate is strictly weaker than the one it replaces. Suggested fix: fetch the merge ref (`git fetch origin "refs/pull/${PR_NUMBER}/merge"` with `pr-number` passed via `init`, then `upstream="$(git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD^1)"`), or correct the commit message/file comment to document the weaker base.

---

**low** — `.rwx/tests.yml`, `.rwx/validate-assets.yml`, `.rwx/trunk-check.yml`, `.rwx/trunk-impacted-targets.yml` (`on.github.pull_request` blocks). The GHA workflows restrict `pull_request` to `branches: [main]`; the RWX ports have no branch restriction, so every PR against *any* base branch will fire all four workflows and post status checks, and `trunk-impacted-targets.yml` will upload impacted targets for non-`main` target branches too. No required-status deadlock (the extra statuses aren't in `required_statuses`), but it produces redundant runs, status noise, and impacts uploads Trunk's queue never consumes. Suggested fix: restrict the PR triggers to `main`-targeted PRs the way the RWX reference/trigger docs allow, or note the deviation in the cutover follow-up.

---

**low** — `.rwx/trunk-impacted-targets.yml` (`upload` task). The GHA workflow handles fork/Dependabot PRs via `secrets.TRUNK_API_TOKEN` resolving to empty and the in-script `-z` guard. The RWX port relies on the same empty-string resolution for `${{ vaults.buridan-ui-trunk.secrets.TRUNK_API_TOKEN }}` when a fork PR's ref doesn't match the locked vault's grants — but the sdk-python-attio reference deliberately gates the vault-touching task with `if:` on `pr-author`, explicitly noting that RWX documents no guarantee about how env resolution behaves when a locked vault doesn't unlock. If RWX fails the task instead of resolving the secret to empty, fork PRs get a red `trunk-impacted-targets` check instead of the intended green skip. Suggested fix: add an author gate (`if: ${{ init.pr-author == 'elviskahoro' }}` with `pr-number`/`pr-author` captured in `init`, as the attio reference does) so the vault is only touched on PRs that can actually unlock it, or verify empirically that a locked-vault miss resolves to empty before the cutover.

The branch is squashed into one commit and rebased onto current `origin/main`, but it isn't pushed and there's no PR yet. The instructions require your approval of the draft before I push.

An earlier squash I did against the freshly fetched `origin/main` bundled in reverts of already-merged fixes. roborev caught it. I reset to the original commits, rebased properly, and re-squashed. The diff is now only the 5 intended files (+290 lines, `.rwx/*.yml` and `.trunk/trunk.yaml`).

I also fixed one roborev finding. `.rwx/trunk-impacted-targets.yml` read `event.github.pull_request.number`, but the sibling RWX repos use the nested `pull_request.pull_request.*` path, so I changed it to match.

I couldn't validate the YAML files because the sandbox has no PyYAML. The repo has no tests covering `.rwx/`, so I ran none.

```text
Title: Stage RWX versions of the CI workflows ahead of the GitHub Actions cutover

Body:
---
## Why
RWX triggers only fire from the default branch, so the RWX ports of the CI workflows have to land on `main` before the GitHub Actions versions can be retired. This stages `.rwx/{tests,trunk-check,validate-assets,trunk-impacted-targets}.yml` alongside the existing workflows, following sdk-python-attio and sdk-python-linear, so the cutover can be validated on real runs. `.trunk/trunk.yaml` excludes `.rwx/**` from checkov, whose `gha-*` rules misfire on RWX env blocks.

## Risks
`merge.required_statuses` is deliberately unchanged, so nothing here gates merges. The workflows only start running once this lands, so expect to tune them on the first real PRs. `pullfrog.yml` stays on GitHub Actions.

## Links
- Follow-up (cutover): GitHub issue, to be created and linked on approval
---

Roborev: 1 round clean of high/medium, 3 low findings unresolved (design-level, not fixed):
1. trunk-check lints the PR head against the merge-base, so a regression on a line main already fixed won't be reported. The GHA version diffs against main's tip.
2. The RWX PR triggers have no `branches: [main]` restriction, unlike the GHA versions.
3. The impacted-targets upload has no author gate, so a fork PR could fail red instead of skipping if RWX errors on a locked-vault miss.

Push and create this PR? (or edit before I submit)
```

On "yes" I'll fetch and rebase, push, run `gh pr create --base main`, and open a follow-up issue for the cutover and the three low findings.
